outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Redesigning the manufacturing footprint to favour a high-yield portfolio concentrated on Premium Motorcycles, Scooters and Electric Vehicles, while continuing to expand market share in commuter motorcycles
- Building supply-chain resilience and customer centricity in the Parts, Accessories & Merchandise (PAM) business through the Global Parts Center (GPC) 2.0 expansion
- Pursuing global growth through an insight-led, hyper-local execution strategy tailored to individual international markets, leaning on joint ventures as growth engines (e.g. Colombia, Bangladesh)
- Scaling and elevating the Hero brand in global markets via product-specific localised launch campaigns and expanded international product portfolio (Xoom, Hunk range)
- Accelerating digital transformation - revamped global digital presence, Lead Management System (LMS) and Dealer Manager System (DMS) deployment for an integrated customer/dealer ecosystem
- Treating AI as a core component of the 'Future of Mobility' strategy, not just a manufacturing-efficiency tool, to sharpen competitive edge
- The Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (published on its website) governing dividend decisions, and follows a two-tranche cadence each year - an interim dividend paid during the year and a final dividend recommended by the Board for shareholder confirmation/declaration at the Annual General Meeting.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is transitioning its legacy manufacturing footprint to be more agile, redesigning capacity to favour a high-yield mix of Premium Motorcycles, Scooters and Electric Vehicles while continuing to grow commuter-motorcycle share. Its manufacturing base comprises six facilities in India (Gurugram, Dharuhera, Halol, Neemrana, Haridwar and Tirupati) plus dedicated overseas plants in Villa Rica, Colombia (its first overseas manufacturing facility) and Jessore, Bangladesh (a joint venture with the Niloy Group), together supporting an approximate annual production capacity of 8.63 million units. A Center for Innovation and Technology (CIT) R&D facility operates at Jaipur, Rajasthan. On the supply-chain side, the Board approved an additional investment for a new Global Parts Center (GPC) 2.0 in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh - featuring Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems, a Centralised Order Management System and Automated Sorters, with a conveyor network spanning over 5 km - to supplement the existing GPC at Neemrana and support the Parts, Accessories & Merchandise (PAM) business. Internationally, the Company achieved a historic export milestone (4,02,786 units, up 40.13% YoY), formally entered Europe (UK, Italy, France and Spain) with a Euro 5+ compliant portfolio, re-launched operations in Sri Lanka, started dispatches to Ecuador, and incorporated a wholly-owned subsidiary in Brazil that is building infrastructure and supply-chain networks for a full-scale commercial launch targeted for FY 2026-27. On the energy side, the Company expanded and planned further captive/wheeled solar power capacity across several plants (Dharuhera, Gurugram, Haridwar, Neemrana, GPC and CIT) as part of its energy-conservation programme.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- GST 2.0 reform (effective September 22, 2025) reclassified sub-350cc two-wheelers from the 28% to 18% tax slab with no sunset clause, providing a permanent structural improvement in affordability that management expects to keep supporting demand
- Recovery in replacement demand for commuter motorcycles, driven by a widening pool of aging vehicles nearing end of operational life plus continued permeation of GST-cut benefits, expected to continue into FY 2026-27
- Premium motorcycle uptrading accelerated by GST rationalisation lowering barriers for first-time buyers, sustained by a strong industry new-launch pipeline
- Rural demand recovery supported by an above-normal South West monsoon (108% of long-period average) and strong nominal wage growth
- Union Budget FY 2026-27 capital expenditure set to rise ~11.5% with continued focus on rural roads and national highways, which management views as structurally positive for mobility demand given the correlation between infrastructure expansion and two-wheeler demand in core segments
- Fiscal stimulus via personal taxation (zero income tax raised to annual incomes up to Rs 1.2 million) augmenting household purchasing power
- Monetary easing - cumulative 125 bps RBI repo rate cut through December 2025 - lowering finance costs for two-wheeler buyers
- EV segment penetration accelerating, aided by extension of the PM E-DRIVE subsidy scheme to July 2026, supporting the Company's VIDA electric business
- RBI has revised FY 2026-27 GDP growth projection down 30 bps to 6.6%, citing West Asia conflict-driven supply disruptions, inflation risk from volatile crude prices and possible weak monsoon (El Nino) as headwinds, though services-sector momentum, GST-rationalisation effects, rising manufacturing capacity utilisation and healthy corporate/financial-institution balance sheets are expected to keep supporting domestic demand

deepdive.thesis: Hero MotoCorp delivered record FY26 revenue and PAT driven by a structural shift to scooters and exports, but faces immediate FY27 margin compression from West Asia-induced commodity spikes (aluminum/fuel) that outpace current 2% price hikes. The strategic pivot involves aggressive capacity doubling in scooters/EV and a ₹1,500 crore capex plan to capture high-growth segments while navigating a transitory profitability dip.
